# rework r3 claims — card_billing_and_disputes (render-source round)

- R1 compute_basis quotes not verbatim → The three quotes are fixed: the line review's payment span, the courtesy relationship spend and the courtesy missed due date. A mechanical sweep now confirms that every compute_basis quote in all five policies is a verbatim substring of its own rule, that every compute binding has a quote, and that every baseline sentence is a sentence of the rule.
- R2 line-review clause with no compute counterpart → The one-account / other-network scope clause is removed from the credit-line-review rule. The base combined-limit rule stays inherited and unchanged, and nothing in the extended rule now lacks a compute counterpart.
- R3 factors resting on another factor's output → Every factor now decides its quantity from its own reads and from plain record reads. The baseline formula of each computation combines the factor outputs. The sweep lists each factor's reads and finds no sibling factor output or binding.
  - utilization_share: the measured-balance rule is folded into this factor's own evidence. Balance measurement is no longer a separate factor.
  - billed_interest_part and unbilled_accrual_span: replaced by an interest-bearing balance (parameter: promotional balance excluded, or excluded disputed amount, or the statement balance), a billing-time fraction (method: day-prorated share, zero, or one, set by when the fee-bearing posting posted) and accrual days (method: from the statement date, from the posting date, or none). The baseline sentence of the notice combines them with the posting in error and the interest base. The earlier grace test, which needed another factor's output, is dropped.
  - missing_credit_proration and missing_credit_accrual: replaced by a missing-credit time fraction and missing-credit accrual days, both decided from the store refund date and the latest statement alone. The tier that compared the credit owed with the statement balance is dropped.
  - coverage_follow: now selects among record values only: the latest statement's printed minimum, its past-due amount, or the missed minimum. The dispute recomputation is a separate method factor, dispute relief, that yields a reduction. The baseline subtracts it and never takes the catch-up amount below the missed minimum.
- R3 factor count and weight (credit line review) → With balance measurement folded in, the line review gained a payment-pattern share (parameter: payments against statement balances in the same span). The recency share became a sliding recency scale (method: per-month sliding share, flat settled share, or full share). Three share values were retuned so that every factor and the history floor bear weight. Every computation still has at least two parameter factors and at least one method factor.
- R4 pinned readings → The rule text now states what compute does. The missing-credit time fraction counts a refund issued on the statement date or within the proration span before it, and a refund dated after the statement falls to the zero tier. The catch-up coverage says outright that a due date already passed is included.
- World (task 0) → The twin foreign postings, their fees, the August and September statements, two payments, the September interest and one added August store purchase were re-laid, so that the twin postings are first billed on the latest statement. This puts every notice factor off its fall-through tier and keeps the on-time streak, the notice window and the netting of the closed dispute.
- Scored values → Task 0 moved: the notice amount and the new credit line both changed, and everything downstream was re-derived (arguments, tracing, computations, sensitivities, closure, solvability, seed checks, rationale). Task 1 did not move: every scored value is unchanged, and only factor names, tier wording and traces were updated.
- Edge probes → These ran on scratch copies, with no error and no change to scored values. No foreign fee, no twin, no statements, no refund, no late fee and no later statement each give the rule's stated result. A closed higher-tier membership, an older foreign fee and an older refund decoy do not move the reads.
- Proof sweep → The proof text of both tasks was re-checked against initial_state: rationale, closures, objective/necessity, factor traces, tracing, solvability and seed checks. Stale figures and old factor names were replaced.
